title: Portugal External Growth 1960-1973
description:
Reproducible research-software repository for constructing source-grounded evidence on Portuguese colonial and European economic linkages between 1960 and 1973.

The repository contains data engineering, validation, provenance, and empirical-readiness code. It intentionally contains no manuscript, causal estimate, publication draft, or narrative conclusion. Current release reports mark the research data as NOT_READY: sectoral-output sources, fixed-European comparisons, product-to-industry mappings, territorial-definition checks, and empirical design matrices remain incomplete.

The pipeline separates immutable raw snapshots, normalised interim tables, and processed analysis tables; writes repository-relative metadata sidecars with SHA-256 hashes and input-artifact hashes; applies time-aware partner-group definitions; and records release-readiness blockers, data dictionaries, source-release policy, and archive manifests. Empirical safeguards include source-registry validation, source-transition checks, materialised output-growth lineage, validated world-total export-growth inputs, and model-specific joined outcome/exposure design checks.

creators.name: Ribeiro, Diogo
creators.affiliation: ESMAD - School of Media Arts and Design, Polytechnic of Porto

method: Install the Python package dependencies with Poetry, then run poetry run peg reproduce-from-local, poetry run peg validate, and the pytest suite. Release reports are generated with poetry run peg freeze-research-data. Network refreshes are intentionally separate from deterministic local reproduction and require provider access where applicable.
notes: The MIT license applies to repository code. Third-party source data, downloaded responses, historical documents, and transcriptions remain subject to the terms, licenses, and access conditions of their original providers. When redistribution rights are unresolved, release archives include metadata, checksums, citations, and derived tables rather than restricted local source documents.
references: Banco de Portugal BPstat Data API. https://bpstat.bportugal.pt/data/docs
